I farm only 3.0 mu, and my family has some off-farm work, so I will keep the plan simple, steady, and easy for me to manage. I will keep wheat-maize as my main system because it fits my land, my experience, and my irrigation conditions, and it gives me stable grain output. I will put 2.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 1.0 mu in cotton because cotton is still familiar to me and helps spread risk. Since I have well irrigation, I will use it at the key stages rather than irrigating too often. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps me get more stable yields, and I will not push fertilizer excessively because my land is small and I want to control costs. For wheat, I will focus on a solid base fertilizer, one topdressing of nitrogen, and a few irrigations around sowing, jointing, and grain filling if needed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer moderate, and rely on fewer irrigations because summer rain helps. For cotton, I will manage it more carefully because it needs a longer season and more pest attention, but on only 1.0 mu I can still handle it myself.
